messages:
maria: Heads-up — trying to cut the sample-app SDK release but typegen produced a change that bumped vendor SDKs to a minor/patch mismatch. Repro steps: `yarn && yarn typegen && git diff`
ben: Ugh. Can you paste the diff?
maria: minimal but important — optional query param ordering ended up with a generated overload that looks like a breaking change in TS consumers:
```diff
- fetch(items: string[], opts?: {timeout?: number, retry?: boolean})
+ fetch(items: string[], retry?: boolean, opts?: {timeout?: number})
```
cassandra: That would surface as a semver-major in TS land if consumers relied on positional args, but our changelog bot only saw a docstring tweak and labeled it as patch. So the changelog and typegen semver disagree. :facepalm:
diego: Why did typegen reorder the optional params? We didn't change API surface in OpenAPI. Could be the codegen reorder heuristic when encountering two optional param groups. Which generator version?
maria: Running `@redwood/typegen` v0.12.3 (published last week). Local diff shows type signature change but no schema change in the openapi.yaml. I suspect a param grouping/optional flattening regression.
regen-bot: PR #4128 opened by @maria — "typegen: preserve param tuple ordering to avoid positional changes" (CI: pending)
ben: CI is failing on the sample-app smoke tests, likely because the packaged SDK now has different call signatures. Deploy blocked until we sort the semver label vs actual breakage.
cassandra: Short term: can we patch typegen to emit the previous ordering? Or revert the package publish for SDKs and force a patch release with coercion? We also need to fix the changelog generator mapping.
diego: I can try a quick fix to prefer original parameter grouping when optional flags are present. If that's low risk we can publish a 0.12.4 patch that restores previous TS overloads. But if consumers legitimately depended on the new ordering we need a minor bump and proper changelog.
maria: For the release cut right now, suggest revert the SDK publish for sample-app and hold the release train. I'll open a revert PR and mark the changelog entry as "manual review" so the bot doesn't autolabel.
ben: Please add a minimal test in the codegen pipeline that asserts stable overload ordering for optional groups. We keep hitting nondeterministic reorders in CI.
diego: ACK — adding a unit test. Also adding a note to typegen changelog explaining the ordering heuristic.
maria: Revert PR is up: https://git.redwood.ai/p/sample-apps/pulls/219 — tagging @cassandra for release decision.
cassandra: I'll hold the release, re-run the release checklist once 0.12.4 is published and changelog corrected. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
maria: Filed followups: 1) add deterministic ordering test in typegen CI, 2) update changelog-bot mapping to treat typegen signature diffs as "semver-impact: review", 3) postmortem if revert happens.
ben: Cool. If anyone hits flakiness in regen diffs, ping me.
diego: Quick note — reproducer in gist: https://gist.github.com/diego/abcdef — includes the openapi fragment and a local `yarn typegen` output.
maria: Closing loop once 0.12.4 patch confirmed and sample-app smoke green. :thumbsup:
